Since the deploy: average throughput for our hot path has oscillated between 60–180 req/s, and p99 has jumped from 220ms to >1.8s. Error rate (5xx) spiked to ~2.1% in the last 30m.

Attached: SLO_Report_Q2.pdf (summary) and spike-logs.zip (samples + klog traces).

- immediate rollback for our tenant to v2.0 OR
- switch to v2.1-fp16 variant + disable qalpha-4bit for our account

Can you confirm whether Redwood can pin us to v2.0 immediately? Procurement is looped for contract/credits.

Thanks —
Raj

Raj / team —

Preliminary triage notes after looking at the attached klogs and KV traces:
- The qalpha-4bit quantization profile introduced a micro-path in the decode kernel that increases CPU backpressure under mid-sized sequences (~120–300 tokens). When the runtime hits the backpressure threshold it begins queuing which shows up as throughput oscillation and spikey p99s.
- There are also decode-time mutex waits with the new fused attention kernel under certain batch sizes — these line up with your logged timestamps.

Short-term mitigations I recommend now:
1) Pin Saffron tenant to v2.0 (as Rishi recommended).
2) If you want to stay on v2.1, switch your account to the fp16 variant (v2.1-fp16) and disable qalpha-4bit until we ship a hotfix. That path will reduce quant-induced stalls at a modest cost increase.
3) Temporarily reduce batching to 4 requests /slot for your hot path — Karthik will push that override.

I’ve uploaded a filtered trace set and a short kernel-level note here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-saffron-logs (read-only).

We’ll prioritize a patch that removes the contention in the fused kernel; ETA for a candidate hotfix is 72 hours pending repro on our internal stress harness.

Irene Choi
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime
irene.choi@redwood.ai
